priorStories.headline: Riyadh airport attack kills 12, injures 309
priorStories.body:
An attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed 12 people and injured 309, Saudi civil aviation authorities said. Some of those injured were in critical condition. The dead included four Saudis and eight foreign nationals, including a U.S. citizen.

Airport operations were suspended, with the closure extended until 9 p.m. Sunday. The Saudi-led coalition blamed the Houthis, who had not claimed responsibility.

priorStories.headline: India detains thousands before election protest
priorStories.body:
Police detained more than 2,000 protesters and leaders of India’s youth-led “Cockroach” movement before a planned demonstration in New Delhi. Authorities also restricted access, transportation and mobile internet in parts of the capital.

The demonstrators were demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a disputed revision of voter lists. India’s government and Election Commission deny allegations that the process is being used to manipulate the rolls.

priorStories.headline: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections to 2027
priorStories.body:
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas canceled legislative elections scheduled for November 28, 2026. His decree instead set simultaneous presidential and legislative elections for September 11, 2027.

The Palestinian presidency cited security, logistical and on-the-ground obstacles to holding the November vote.

priorStories.headline: Simon nears Mexico with 155 mph winds
priorStories.body:
Hurricane Simon’s maximum sustained winds reached 155 mph as its eyewall approached Mexico’s west-central coast. The Category 4 storm was moving north at 5 mph at 9 p.m. CST.

The National Hurricane Center warned that conditions would deteriorate rapidly within the hurricane-warning area.

priorStories.headline: Hurricane Isaias linked to four deaths
priorStories.body:
Authorities linked at least four deaths in Florida and Alabama to Hurricane Isaias. Two people died when trees fell on homes, one died from carbon monoxide produced by a generator, and another died in a vehicle crash involving a downed tree.

The post-tropical system continued to bring flood and wind hazards across the Southeast and toward the Appalachians.

candidates.summary: Indian authorities released Cockroach Janata Party leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, one day after detaining them before a New Delhi demonstration over voter-list revisions. The movement’s legal director said their release was conditioned on committing no breach of peace for one year; it was unclear how that condition would affect future protest activity. Police also detained protesters during demonstrations Sunday.
candidates.title: India releases leaders of youth protest movement

candidates.summary: Yemen’s Houthis renewed threats against Saudi aviation after the deadly attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport. A Houthi military spokesman said Saudi airports were targets and urged people to heed the group’s warnings. The Saudi-led coalition has blamed the Houthis for the airport attack, while the group had not claimed responsibility for that strike.
candidates.title: Houthis renew threats against Saudi airports

candidates.summary: Pope Leo XIV announced during his Sunday Angelus that he will undergo surgery in the coming days to remove a lung nodule discovered during recent medical checks. He said it was detected at a very early stage and was well-localized. The Vatican said the operation is expected early this week at Rome’s Gemelli hospital, with hospitalization lasting about one week.
candidates.title: Pope Leo XIV announces surgery for lung nodule

candidates.summary: The International Organization for Migration said Sunday that at least 139 migrants had died and 84 remained missing after an overcrowded boat carrying 305 people capsized off Djibouti during the night of October 8-9. More than 80 people survived. The vessel was traveling toward Yemen, and rescue work continued.
candidates.title: IOM reports 139 dead in Djibouti migrant shipwreck

candidates.summary: Polish authorities arrested a man suspected of threatening an attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk after police received information concerning possible attacks on Tusk and Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. Security officials held an emergency meeting and said they treated the threat as having a high probability of being carried out. Officials disclosed no details about the suspect or the alleged plan.
candidates.title: Poland arrests man over alleged threat to prime minister

candidates.summary: A projectile struck a passenger terminal at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport, causing injuries, the Saudi-led coalition said. The Houthis claimed responsibility for this strike and the previous day’s deadly attack. India’s embassy said one of its citizens died Sunday from injuries sustained Saturday, raising that attack’s toll to 13. Saudi authorities also reported an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam without providing details.
candidates.title: Houthis claim new attacks on Saudi airports

candidates.summary: Hurricane Simon pounded Mexico’s Pacific coast while remaining just offshore as a Category 4 storm. By midday Sunday, its eye was about 65 miles from Cabo Corrientes, with sustained winds near 140 mph. Jalisco authorities evacuated people from high-risk areas, and forecasters warned of catastrophic winds, life-threatening storm surge, flooding and mudslides along west-central Mexico.
candidates.title: Hurricane Simon pounds Mexico’s Pacific coast
